title: Treadmill-based gait analysis
summary: Measuring how people walk using video, OpenCV and biomechanics. I built the video-processing pipeline without a pose-estimation library for my bachelor’s thesis.
finding: I built the video-processing pipeline for a completed team gait-analysis project. The wider system combined camera-based kinematics with MPU motion sensors and force-sensitive resistors (FSRs). GitHub contains the video-analysis portion; the MPU and FSR work is documented in the full thesis report.

title: Healthcare Nanochat
summary: Preparing medical conversations for a language model, then running the training workflow on a supercomputer. My work covered data curation, preprocessing and tokenization.
finding: I worked on the data preparation and tokenization workflow and was responsible for running the pipeline on the HPC supercomputer. This gave me practical experience with Apptainer and the operational side of model training.
stack: Dataset curation · BPE tokenization · HPC · Apptainer

title: Brain tumour segmentation
summary: A fellowship team project teaching a model to outline brain tumours in MRI scans. I contributed modality analysis, literature review and augmentation research.
finding: I contributed literature review, analysis of MRI modalities and data augmentation research. The team baseline achieved approximately 0.72 mean Dice, giving me practical grounding in how preprocessing, training and evaluation fit together.
stack: 3D U-Net · Multimodal MRI · BraTS2021 · Dice evaluation

title: US flight delay pipeline
summary: Following more than a million flight records from raw files to an interactive dashboard. My first data-engineering project, inspired by airplanes and geography.
finding: The project report documents 1,087,018 flight records across January 2024 and January 2025, with source checksums, rejected-record tracking, safe reruns and explicit metric denominators. My focus was learning how to build a robust pipeline across its stages.
stack: PySpark · HDFS · MongoDB · Plotly Dash · Data lineage

title: Whole-slide image preprocessing
summary: Turning very large liver tissue scans into useful image patches. I maintained the pipeline across operating systems and ran it on HPC: about 85 seconds for the reported slide.
finding: I maintained the workflow across macOS, Windows and Linux, resolved library compatibility problems and was responsible for running the project on the supercomputer with Apptainer. The team report evaluates tissue masking on 369 liver WSIs.

title: Liver segmentation with U-Net
summary: A completed Advanced Machine Learning assignment teaching a model to mark the liver in CT images, so its predicted outline can be compared with a reference outline.
finding: The U-Net model reached a best validation Dice score of 0.8962. This measures overlap between the predicted liver region and the reference region. Images from each patient were kept in the same data split to reduce leakage.
stack: U-Net · CT images · PyTorch · Image segmentation

title: Generalizable ECG classification
summary: Exploring how a model recognizes patterns in heart signals—and what changes when it encounters signals from a different dataset.
finding: The work explores class balancing, signal augmentation, attention and gradient-based visualizations, noise robustness and external-dataset evaluation. The notebook reports approximately 0.63 PTB-XL test macro F1; cross-dataset transfer remains a limitation.
stack: CNN–Transformer · ECG · Class imbalance · Robustness evaluation

title: Early sepsis prediction
summary: Using patient measurements and recent changes to estimate sepsis severity two, four and six hours ahead.
finding: The notebook combines 43 clinical variables with eight temporal trend features and reports mean AUROC values of 0.795, 0.794 and 0.791 across the three horizons. The evaluation partition also selects the early-stopping checkpoint, so these are exploratory coursework results rather than independent test estimates.
stack: PyTorch · Clinical time series · Multitask learning · Feature importance
course: Applied Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence (CM2011)

title: Clinical alarm classification
summary: A coursework study asking whether recorded patient signals can help distinguish real clinical alarms from false alarms.
finding: The notebook compares logistic regression and random forests using measurements extracted from waveforms, explores ways to fill missing values, and evaluates precision and recall under class imbalance.
stack: Clinical waveforms · Random forests · Missing data · Scikit-learn
course: Applied Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence (CM2011)

title: Chest X-ray report classification
summary: A model that reads the written report accompanying a chest X-ray and identifies three types of findings. It connects medical imaging with clinical language processing.
finding: The coursework compares a BiLSTM with simpler text-classification baselines, separates patients across data splits, and reports test macro F1 of 0.80 for the BiLSTM at a 0.5 threshold. The inputs are report text, not X-ray pixels.
stack: Radiology reports · Clinical NLP · BiLSTM · MIMIC-CXR

title: Autograd from scratch
summary: A small learning exercise building automatic differentiation and a simple neural network to understand how training calculates and follows gradients.
finding: The notebook moves from manual derivatives to a graph of arithmetic operations and automatic backpropagation, following educational references including Karpathy’s micrograd.

title: Urban data integration
summary: Bringing taxi trips, weather, air quality and geography together, then measuring how storage choices affect the pipeline.
finding: The repository documents 8,480,836 accepted trips and a measured comparison of partitioned versus flat storage. The work explores validated ingestion, contextual joins and workload-dependent performance trade-offs, with substantial ChatGPT assistance during development.
stack: PySpark · Delta Lake · Data integration · Storage benchmarking

title: Federated activity recognition
summary: A small coursework project exploring how a shared model can learn to recognize activities while each participant’s sensor data stays in its own partition.
finding: I worked through the full implementation using Flower, comparing ways of combining local models and adding differential privacy on HARBox and IMU activity data.
stack: Flower · Sensor data · Federated learning · Differential privacy
course: Federated Computing Privacy and Security for Health Data (CM2028)

title: Fantasy Premier League analytics
summary: I enjoy Fantasy Premier League, so I used its data to explore the players behind the game: their teams, national representation and age distributions.
finding: The substantive notebook joins player and team data, explores player backgrounds and plots age and birth-date distributions. This is a personal data exploration; predictive models and a dashboard are not implemented in the reviewed source.
stack: Python · Pandas · Seaborn · APIs · FPL data

title: Biomedical engineers in Nepal
summary: An early coding exercise: collecting public biomedical-engineering registration listings in Nepal to practise web scraping and explore the resulting data.
finding: A small learning exercise in gathering and organizing data. The repository describes its registration snapshot as current to 9 October 2024.
presentation: Brief note with source link; no dedicated case study in final layout

title: MATLAB polling machine
summary: An early MATLAB project building a graphical interface for casting votes—a small exercise in connecting user actions with program logic.
finding: The repository contains the MATLAB application code and GUI figure. A separate project report is available among the collected engineering reports.

title: Federated learning for hospitals
summary: Exploring whether a small hospital benefits from a shared prediction model. My contribution was preparing the clinical data.
finding: The study compared local, pooled and federated models for a simulated small hospital. Non-private global models improved utility over local-only training; the membership-inference attack was already near chance, limiting conclusions about additional attack reduction from differential privacy.
stack: Clinical data preprocessing · Federated learning · Privacy evaluation

title: Pacemaker control simulation
summary: An early team project using MATLAB and Simulink to explore how a feedback controller could adjust a simulated pacemaker–heart system as activity changes.
finding: The report models the heart, pacemaker and activity sensor, tunes a PID controller and examines responses to different input signals. It is a simulation study, not a physical medical device.
presentation: Brief entry; no large case study

title: Smart Healthy Chair
summary: An early team hardware project using a distance sensor and Arduino to alert a seated person when their back moves beyond a set distance from the chair.
finding: The report documents circuit design in Proteus, a printed circuit board, and buzzer and LED alerts. It is a simple distance-based posture reminder, not a comprehensive posture assessment system.
stack: Arduino · Ultrasonic sensor · Proteus · PCB design
